meta.notes: TUSCANY CROSSING 103K CYCLE - nutrition (rev 2.3). 29 weeks, 9/28/2026 -> 4/18/2027, matched to run_plan rev 2.3.1 / strength_plan rev 2.3 subtypes (run plan rebuilt from W5 on Uphill Athlete week types; Oracle 50M replaced by the Sun 2/21 long effort). Arnon: 50 M, 175 lb / 79 kg. || THE PROBLEM TO SOLVE (FR-w): at Vermont the gut signalled FULL at ~365 cal/hr by hour 4 (gels every 25 min + half-strength drink + 500 ml/hr); he then ran on gels alone at ~240 cal/hr with no energy cost to 6:40. Tuscany is a ~15:40-17:00 planning day. The fix is the calorie MIX - more solids, less concentrated liquid carbohydrate - not more volume. Target race intake ~260-300 cal/hr, from ~50% gels / ~25% half-strength drink / ~25% real food. THE DRINK = GU Roctane Energy Drink Mix (own powder, carried pre-portioned), taken on top of the GU Roctane gels for carbs AND sodium: half-strength = ~125 kcal / ~31 g carbs / ~160 mg sodium per 500 ml. Any substitute has to replace both. || GUT-TRAINING LADDER (long_run notes + overrides): Base W3-13 proven protocol + one real-food item per long run from W7 | Build W14-22 the MIX at 250-280 cal/hr, cup drinking at car stops; 1/17 = real-food rehearsal for 2/21 | LONG EFFORT 2/21 = J-2, the real-food rehearsal on an 8-10 h day (car = aid every ~2-2.5 h; real food from hour 3; drink-mix replacement tested; every item logged for RS) | Peak: race protocol v1 on 3/7, final on 3/21, nothing new after. One new variable per run; hour 1 always on the proven baseline. || STATION FLUID vs OWN MIX (Arnon's question): with powder pre-portioned per bottle, mixing your own at a cup-only aid costs roughly 20-40 s more than taking station drink - small next to the dwell Vermont actually lost (~4 min of crew chat and toilet queue). The bigger variable is the gut: the station product at Tuscany is unknown (race documents should list it - open item), and your own mix is proven over two ultras. DEFAULT: own powder + station water; station coke/tea/broth as late-race additions only after they pass in training. With Oracle gone there is no aid station before Tuscany, so station drink vs own powder CANNOT be tested head-to-head - the default stands unless the race documents name a product Arnon can buy and trial in March. Coke and broth are trialled at the car on 2/21. || SODIUM & FLUID BY TEMPERATURE (not a flat rate): < 12 C -> 400-600 mg Na/hr, 400-500 ml/hr (no scheduled SaltStick) | 12-22 C -> 600-800 mg, 500-650 ml (SaltStick 1/60 min) | > 22 C -> 800-1,000 mg, 650-800 ml (SaltStick 1/40-45 min). Tuscany's regulation warns of near 0 C at night and > 30 C midday. Indoor treadmill sessions usually sit in the middle tier. || EARLY-START FUELING: Tuscany breakfast lands at ~02:45-03:00. Rehearsed on 11/22 (04:00) and 2/21 (03:00, identical to race timing - now the opening of the long effort). || CAFFEINE for a dark finish: tested at dusk on 1/10, late in the day on the 2/21 long effort, and in the March rehearsals; race cap ~5 mg/kg (~400 mg). || DAILY EATING: protein 1.8-1.9 g/kg (~145-155 g) every day including rest days - tendon remodeling at 50 is protein-hungry. Carbs scale with the day (~3.3 g/kg rest -> ~8 g/kg on the biggest long runs; day-type phase_adjustments raise totals as run hours climb from ~6.8 h (W5) to 13.4 h (W25); recovery weeks W6, 9, 11, 13, 17, 22 run 4-6 h - eat to base targets there; W21 is 12.1 h, mostly Sunday). ENERGY AVAILABILITY: weekly hours roughly double from October to March - if body weight drifts down > ~1.5 kg, or sleep, mood or resting HR worsen, eat more before training less. COLLAGEN 15 g + vitamin C 250 mg 30-60 min before every Lower A/B session, otherwise with the morning foot routine. NO NSAIDs around loading. Alcohol: Friday evening is the window in normal weeks (36 h before a Sunday long run; in back-to-back weeks the Saturday medium-long follows - keep it to one drink); none the night before the 2/21 long effort (Saturday 2/20) and none in Tuscany race week. || AeT TESTS: nutrition is held identical at every drift test (10/13, 11/24, 1/19 - moved from 1/5; the 2/16 test is dropped) so the only variable is fitness. || FRIDAYS (rev 2.3): Friday is a run day in every week (fast-feet run, subtype easy, 3-4.5 mi), so Friday resolves to easy_run_upper_swim, which now carries the back-to-back-weekend carb note. strength_only_swim fires only on swim + upper days without a run (W10 Friday, W11/W13 Saturdays, W21 Friday). || SWIM DAYS (rev 2.1): three day types resolve Total Immersion swim days (Monday swim-only; swim + Upper B with or without a run). They are listed FIRST because triggers are first-match: a trigger with cross_subtype matches only when that cross session is scheduled; a trigger without cross_subtype ignores cross sessions (backward compatible). Easy swim ~250-400 kcal. || date_overrides are the source of truth on test, gate, headlamp, rehearsal, long-effort, carb-load and race days.

session_fueling.notes: HOURS 1-2 (dark, cold): gels + half-strength mix only, the proven baseline. FROM HOUR 3: one real-food item every ~45 min. DRINK-MIX REPLACEMENT: from ~hour 6 run one full car loop with the GU Roctane drink replaced by plain water in the bottles plus an equal carb AND sodium dose from other sources - each half-strength bottle you drop is ~125 kcal / ~31 g carbs and ~160 mg sodium, so cover it with ~250 ml cola in the cup at the car (~105 kcal) plus broth or a salted potato for the sodium (SaltStick if neither). Rate the gut over the next hour vs the loop before. This is the fallback if the Roctane drink turns cloying late in the race. CAFFEINE: none before hour 5, then one caffeinated gel every ~90 min, total <= ~200 mg; log alertness. CAR STOPS: timed, <= 2 min, set list (bottles, food, out); drink one cup at every stop (Tuscany aid is cup-only). Sodium/fluid by temperature tier (likely the cold tier until mid-morning). INTAKE LOG for RS, every item: time, item, ~cal, ~sodium, GI notes; gut fullness 0-10 each hour.
Rehydrate ~150% of the weight lost, with sodium. Body report to RS at the finish.

fueling_schedule.item: GU Roctane Energy Drink Mix, half-strength in 500 ml (own powder, pre-portioned)
Real food: own carried items + station bread/fruit/broth/coke later

session_fueling.notes: MIX, not volume (FR-w): gels ~50%, half-strength drink ~25%, real food ~25%. CAFFEINE: none for the first ~6 h; then ~35-70 mg every 1.5-2 h from the Mountain climb (~hour 8), a larger dose before dusk; total <= ~5 mg/kg (~400 mg). Carry own powder pre-portioned per bottle; use station water. Refill both bottles + 1 L minimum before the long carries (into Gallina 9.9 mi, Poggio Rosa 8.0 mi).

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.notes: Autumn blood work suggested (25-OH vitamin D, ferritin, CBC) before the winter volume block - dose by result. Do not supplement iron without a low ferritin result.

supplements.name: Omega-3 fish oil (EPA/DHA)
supplements.rationale: Anti-inflammatory support without blunting adaptation (unlike NSAIDs, which stay OFF around loading).

supplements.name: Collagen peptides + Vitamin C
supplements.timing: 30-60 min BEFORE lower/tendon strength sessions; on non-lifting days, with the morning foot-corrective block
supplements.rationale: Peri-loading collagen availability for tendon remodeling — the P1 nutritional lever. Daily low-dose beats one big weekly dose because collagen synthesis has a refractory window.
supplements.notes: THE priority supplement this block. Never skipped on Lower A / Lower B days.

supplements.name: Creatine monohydrate
supplements.timing: post-run or post-strength, any consistent daily slot
supplements.rationale: Strength/power support during the HSR block; consistency matters more than timing.

supplements.name: Whey protein isolate
supplements.timing: post-session windows and to top up daily protein
supplements.rationale: Hits the 1.7-1.9 g/kg/day protein target that tissue remodeling at 50 demands.

supplements.name: Magnesium glycinate
supplements.rationale: Sleep quality — recovery is the P1 multiplier.

supplements.name: Electrolytes (SaltStick)
supplements.dose: Temperature-tiered: < 12 C none scheduled (gel + mix cover it); 12-22 C 1 capsule/60 min; > 22 C 1 capsule/40-45 min
supplements.rationale: Vermont sodium (515-675 mg/hr) was deliberately low for 56 F and caused no cramping; Tuscany's 0-30 C swing needs a tiered rate, not a flat one.

supplements.name: Caffeine (GU Roctane caffeine gels)
supplements.dose: 35 mg per caffeinated gel. Training runs > 3 h: 1-3 in the final third. Evening/dark sessions: one at dusk (test). Race: see the 4/17 override (<= ~400 mg total).
supplements.timing: Final third of long efforts; dusk on headlamp runs
supplements.rationale: Vermont: 3 caffeinated gels in the last 2.5 h, clean. Tuscany adds a 15-17 h day and a dark finish - timing is tested on 1/10, 2/21, 3/7, 3/21.
